12-WEEKHYPERTROPHY

Blocks3 × 4 Weeks
DeloadsWeeks 4, 8 & 12
Days / Week4 flexible days
EquipmentBarbell · DB · Bands
Available Equipment
Standard Barbell (45 lbs)
  • 2× 45 lbs
  • 2× 35 lbs
  • 2× 25 lbs
  • 2× 10 lbs
  • 2× 5 lbs
EZ Curl Bar (35 lbs)
  • 2× 25 lbs
  • 6× 10 lbs
  • 2× 5 lbs
  • 2× 2.5 lbs
Dumbbells (per pair)
  • 3, 5, 8, 10, 15 lbs
  • 20, 25, 30, 40 lbs
Resistance Bands
  • Light
  • Medium
  • Heavy
Loop Bands (5 levels)
  • Light → X-Heavy
  • Pull-up assistance
  • Activation work
Program Structure
Weeks 1–4
Block 1
Foundation
Re-establish movement patterns at 85–95% of your current bests. Higher reps, controlled technique. Week 4 is a full deload.
Sets: 3–4  ·  Reps: 6–10  ·  Intensity: 85–95%
Weeks 5–8
Block 2
Accumulation
Build toward and slightly beyond current bests. Lower rep targets, heavier weights. Week 8 is a deload before the peak block.
Sets: 3–4  ·  Reps: 5–8  ·  Intensity: 92–102%
Weeks 9–12
Block 3
Intensification
Peak performance block. Heaviest working weights. Target new PRs on weeks 10–11. Week 12 is the final deload.
Sets: 4  ·  Reps: 4–6  ·  Intensity: 97–108%

Program Notes
Logging Your Sets
  • Enter the actual weight and reps for every set as you complete it. Hit ✓ to mark a set done.
  • All data is saved automatically in your browser and persists between sessions.
  • The progress bar at the top of each week counts how many exercises have been fully logged.
  • Aim to have all 4 days completed within each calendar week.
Using Target Weights
  • Target weights are working set recommendations — warm up with 2 lighter sets first on all compound lifts.
  • If you hit the top of the rep range across all sets, add the next available weight increment next week.
  • If you can't reach the bottom of the rep range, drop weight and rebuild. Log what you actually did.
  • On deload weeks, complete the prescribed sets but do not push intensity.
Band Progression
  • Resistance bands (lateral raise, face pull, tricep): progress light → medium → heavy as shown each block.
  • Loop bands for pull-up assist: heavier = more assistance = easier. Goal is to reduce assistance each block.
  • Loop bands for activation work: increase tension level as exercises feel too easy.
Equipment Ceilings
  • Incline DB, goblet squat, and Arnold press are capped at 40 lbs per dumbbell. At the ceiling: add pause reps or slow eccentrics.
  • DB row and chest-supported row use 40 lbs from the start. Progress with tempo rather than weight.
  • Skull crushers on the EZ curl bar — you have capacity to reach 95 lbs total.
  • Calf raises start bodyweight, then add a dumbbell as prescribed from week 5.
